lane: THE WELDED SHAPE SHOWING THROUGH A TOWER — case construction for an owner ruling (read-only probe)
summary: The owner's observation is REAL, LIVE and already documented as an open call — `SPARK_CANON.md:388-390` records it verbatim as "the owner's call whether a weld should be swallowed by the building". A "welded shape" is not its own entity type: it is an ordinary `Primitive` that a player free-placed within `AUTO_BOND_RADIUS` (60 px, `constants.ts:824`) of a node the tower stands on, so the auto-bond picked that node and joined them. It is same-colour only (`controls.ts` `pickPrimitiveInRange` rejects `p.placerColor !== myColor`), so a weld on your tower is always your own shape. It IS on the canon ladder — but at `PRIMITIVE_MAX_HP` 70 fifths, NOT the lone-shape 5: `damage.ts:224` clamps to 5 only when `prim.bonds.size === 0`, and a weld has a bond. It is also not an acquisition target at all (`creatureAI.ts:267` skips any prim with bonds), so only area damage reaches it — while its BOND is a perfectly ordinary chewable connector (`findNearestBondTarget` filters on ownership and nothing else). It shows through for ONE reason and it is not render order: render order is correct (shapes at `main.ts:618`, tower sprites at :774/:804/:832, so sprites are on top). The shape is at full alpha because `coverAlphaForPrim` returns 1 for anything the renderers never published (`towerCover.ts:228`), and every publish site excludes the weld DELIBERATELY — `ringBondsOf` at `towerRenderer.ts:79` says in as many words "BOTH ENDPOINTS MUST BE RING MEMBERS … hiding it would erase a connector the tower does not stand on". Crucially, only TWO of the five topologies can even reach this: the 12 race towers + tier-9 (where R136 deliberately permits the weld) and a weld onto a LEAF of a star ramp tower. A weld onto a star's HUB kills the tower (`starShape.ts:108`), and ANY weld kills the pentagram (`pentagram.ts` component-size-5/degree-2), so the structure most people would picture cannot produce this at all. There is NO prior owner ruling on it: the archive, the canon and every handoff carry it as owed, never answered.

findings.claim: It is NOT a render-order defect. Pixi z-order is addChild order and the shapes are added first, so the tower sprite is correctly on top. The shape shows through because it is drawn at alpha 1, not because it is drawn late.

The mechanism: cover is a PUBLISHED set, and anything not published reads alpha 1. structureRenderer applies that alpha to every shape it draws, so an unpublished weld draws fully opaque under the sprite.

THE CRUX — the exclusion is deliberate and has a stated reason. `ringBondsOf` refuses any bond with an endpoint outside the ring, on the grounds that hiding it would erase a connector the tower is not standing on. This is the sentence the owner is being asked to overrule.

fix_shape:
NO FIX SHOULD BE WRITTEN BEFORE THE RULING. What the ruling costs, per option:

⛔ THE ONE HARD CONSTRAINT, whichever he picks: the COVER SET must be widened separately from the MEMBER WALK. `rampMembersAt` (structureRamp.ts:484) is shared by four consumers — sprite placement (`cx`/`cy`), the click box (`rampAnchorAtPoint`), the laser muzzle (`rampMuzzleAt`) and the health fraction (`bonds.length` + `bankedFifths` → `rampHealthFrac`). Adding the weld to `members`/`bonds` would move the building, move its muzzle, move its hit box and re-price its health in one edit. Same for `ring` in towerRenderer.ts (it feeds the centroid and `towerHpFrac`). So the shape of any fix is a NEW, cover-only helper — e.g. `coverExtrasOf(world, members)` returning one-hop neighbours + their bonds — passed as extra arguments to `markTowerCover`, with the member walks left byte-identical.

OPTION A — LEAVE IT (status quo). Cost: 0 files. On screen: your own stray shape and its connector stay bright under the building, exactly what he reported. Breaks nothing.

OPTION B — SWALLOW ONE HOP. Cover any prim bonded directly to a covered member, plus that bond. ~15 lines in a new helper + 3 call sites (towerRenderer.ts:312, structureRampRenderer.ts:223, voltkinTowerRenderer.ts:576) + tests. On screen: the tower reads clean. Cost in play: a chewable connector goes invisible — consistent with R183-F, which he already ruled ("it doesn't matter if you know what connectors to cut"), and raids still work because the raid pick never consults cover alpha. ⚠ THE REAL RISK: shared leaves are legal (starShape.ts documents two stars sharing a Circle), so one hop out from tower A can hide a shape that is tower B's leaf. If B has no art, B becomes a blank patch of board — the exact defect towerCover.ts:17-26 exists to prevent.

OPTION C — SWALLOW WHAT IS UNDER THE ART. Cover a neighbour only if its position falls inside the sprite's drawn box (T3 art is 84 px square, towerFrames.ts:131; AUTO_BOND_RADIUS is 60). ~20 lines, same call sites. On screen: nothing pokes out from under the building; anything standing clear of it stays visible and readable. This is the option that matches the literal complaint ("shows THROUGH") without hiding shapes the building is not covering, and it cannot blank a distant structure.

OPTION D — REFUSE THE WELD. A keep-out disc around a built tower's members at placement, like the S182 castle keep-out. This is NOT a render change — it touches placement legality, i.e. the sim. Cost in play: he loses build space around every tower. ⛔ On race towers it would REVERSE R136, which he ruled after being shown the measurement. Note the asymmetry that already exists: `stampRefusalAt` already refuses a blueprint STAMP within 60 px of any primitive; only hand-placed single shapes can weld.

OPTION E — FADE, DON'T HIDE. Give a non-member neighbour a partial alpha (e.g. 0.3) instead of 0. Smallest visual change, keeps the connector legible, keeps the weld's "this is not part of the tower" reading. ~5 lines on top of B or C.

⭐ WORTH PUTTING TO HIM WITH THE RULING: the weld already costs him two things he has probably not connected to this. A welded hub's health bar reads 48% while the art reads 32% and it detonates (R182-F, canon:576), and ONE welded shape makes the whole structure permanently unrepairable (canon §8, structureRepair.ts:151). If he dislikes welds generally, Option D answers all three at once; if he only dislikes the look, C or E is the cheap answer and the other two stay open.
four_sites_risk:
NONE for the render options (A/B/C/E). `towerCover` is renderer-only by construction — its own docblock states "Nothing here is simulated, and nothing COULD have been … this costs no sim state, no snapshot bytes and no PROTOCOL_VERSION bump" (towerCover.ts:10-15). No factory, no serialize, no hash, no worker, no PROTOCOL_VERSION (47) impact. Determinism is unaffected: alpha never feeds the sim, and creature targeting/raid picking never consult cover alpha.

⚠ TWO NON-OBVIOUS HAZARDS IF SOMEONE TAKES A SHORTCUT:
1. Widening `rampMembersAt` or `ring` instead of adding a cover-only helper WOULD reach the sim-adjacent surface — `rampHealthFrac` drives the damage-ramp frame and the self-destruct threshold, which is synced-health-derived presentation two peers must agree on. Keep the member walks byte-identical.
2. If a cover helper iterates `world.bonds` / `Primitive.bonds` (a Set, insertion order) and lets that order decide ANYTHING beyond set membership, it re-enters the S155 N1 class. Membership-only is safe; any ordering must be an explicit id sort.

⛔ OPTION D IS THE ONE THAT IS NOT RENDERER-ONLY. A placement keep-out is a legality predicate — host-authoritative, replay-visible, and it reverses owner ruling R136 on the race towers. That is a sim change and needs its own scope.
tests_owed:
Whichever way he rules, the ruling needs a tripwire — today there is none, and this project's own rule is that a number or behaviour lands with its assertion in the same commit.

1. ⛔ A BEHAVIOURAL TEST, NOT A SOURCE-TEXT GUARD. S182's lesson (CLAUDE.md §2) is that a source-text tripwire proves a line EXISTS, not that it is REACHED. The test must build a world with a live tier-3 race tower, weld a foreign-type shape onto a ring node, run the publish, and assert `coverAlphaForPrim(weldId)` / `coverAlphaForBond(weldBondId)` — 1 if he rules LEAVE IT, ramping to 0 if he rules SWALLOW.
2. A companion assertion that the member walks did NOT move: `rampMembersAt(...).members.length`, `.bonds.length` and `cx`/`cy` unchanged by the presence of a weld, so a future edit cannot widen the cover set through the shared walk.
3. If Option B or C ships: a SHARED-LEAF case — two stars sharing a Circle, one with art and one without — asserting the art-less structure's shapes stay visible. This is the failure mode towerCover.ts:17-26 was written against and it is the one that would ship green otherwise.
4. Extend the existing publish-site census (towerCover.test.ts:267) to count the cover-extras call sites the same way, so a fifth publish site cannot land without one.
5. If Option D ships: a legality test that a hand-placed shape is refused inside the keep-out AND that R136's ringShape.test.ts:106/117 cases are explicitly re-decided rather than silently broken.
6. ⚠ NOTE THE STRUCTURAL LIMIT, stated in the canon at §7b: no renderer runs under vitest, so z-order and actual pixels are invisible to the unit suite. Alpha is testable; "does it look swallowed" is a browser-pane or owner-eye check, and the browser pane never advances world.tick, so it proves static truths only.
owner_questions: A welded shape is ALWAYS your own shape, dropped within 60 px of a tower node so it auto-bonded on. When it sits under the building: should it (a) stay visible as it does now, (b) be swallowed completely along with its connector, or (c) be swallowed only where it is actually under the building's art, and stay visible where it sticks out?

If it is swallowed, its connector goes invisible too — and that connector IS attackable, it just does not count toward the tower's health. You already ruled that hidden connectors are fine because you cannot aim your spawn anyway (R183-F). Does that ruling cover this connector as well, or does a connector that is NOT part of the tower deserve to stay visible so you can see it being eaten?

Two things a weld already does that you may not have connected to this: on a welded hub the health bar reads 48% while the building art reads 32% and it blows up (R182-F), and ONE welded shape makes the whole structure permanently unrepairable — FIX refuses it forever. Would you rather we stop shapes from welding onto a built tower at all? That answers all three at once, but it costs you build space around every tower and it reverses R136, where you deliberately allowed a stray shape to touch a race tower's ring without killing it.

Scope check before anything is built: this can only happen on the 12 race towers, the tier-9 towers, and on a LEAF of the lightning hub / goblin tower / laser turret / HELGA's hall. A weld onto a hub kills that tower outright, and ANY weld kills a pentagram. Is the ruling for all of those at once, or do you want the race towers treated differently since R136 is what lets them survive a weld in the first place?
size_estimate: Micro for this probe (read-only, no edit owed — the lane's deliverable is the ruling case, and it is complete). The FOLLOW-UP depends entirely on his answer: Option A is zero; Options B/C/E are Micro-to-Standard (~15-25 lines in one new cover-only helper, 3 existing `markTowerCover` call sites, plus 3-4 tests — 10-20K, 4-6 files); Option D is Standard-to-Full because it is a placement-legality change that reverses R136 and needs its own deliberation.
